newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Cyprus stocks move lower at end of week's trade.
newsitem.headline: Cyprus stocks move lower at end of week's trade.

text.p: The Cypriot stock market continued its downward trend on Friday, showing a weekly loss of 1.53 points, or 1.80 percent.
The 41-share Cyprus Stock Exchange (CSE) general share index, which is set at 100 points, has shed 5.43 percent of its value in two weeks, falling to 83.22 on Friday.
Traders and businessmen said the fall was fuelled by widespread rumours of a planned Turkish military operation on the divided island, subsequently dismissed by the government.
Turkey has occupied the northern third of Cyprus since 1974, when it invaded in the wake of a short-lived coup in Nicosia engineered by the military regime ruling Greece at the time.
Last Friday the CSE index closed at 84.75 points.
Weekly turnover was valued at 1.95 million pounds ($4.23 million) compared with 2.82 million pounds between September 9 and 13.
The Cyprus Investment and Securities Corporation (CISCO) said in its weekly report that the banking sector contributed most to the market's retreat.
The half yearly earnings reported by banks listed on the stock market appeared to be below investors expectations, CISCO said.

But it said that given the slowdown of the economy this year the 12 to 13 percent growth achieved by the two major banks should be considered satisfactory, referring to results of the Bank of Cyprus and the Cyprus Popular Bank.
A third Cypriot bank, Hellenic, announced an increase in its half yearly pre-tax profit by 20.4 percent to 2.63 million pounds from 2.187 in the first half of 1995.
The banking sub index closed at 89.95 points, shedding 1.59 points, or 1.73 percent from last Friday's close of 91.54.
Fully paid shares of the Bank of Cyprus closed lower at 339 shedding 8.5 cents from Friday's close. The Cyprus Popular Bank closed at 322 from last week's close of 323.
On Tuesday the Popular Bank released its six month results showing an increase in pre-tax profit of 13.2 percent to 18.20 million pounds compared to 16.08 million pounds last year.
The Hellenic Bank closed at 248.5 from last week's close of 257.5.
The sub index of insurance companies closed at 61.88, losing gains it made in the early trading days of the week and closing slightly higher than last Friday's close of 61.62. ($=0.46 pounds)
